requestedActions.title: Read titles of work packages the connected person can access
Connect a customer's own OpenProject instance via OAuth using the instance base URL

guide.summary: OpenProject documents an OAuth authorization code flow and a GET work package list with offset pagination. The documented api_v3 scope is a broad standard API grant, not a work-package-only scope, and no read-only enforcement is documented, so the boundary must be checked by request logs. Customer-instance registration and distribution policy remain unknown. Execution is untested.

findings.title: Authorization code flow for user-level OAuth
findings.detail: The authorization URL takes client_id, redirect_uri, scope and prompt=consent, and the returned code is exchanged at the token URL. The documented hosts are example.com placeholders, so use the customer instance base URL.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to connecting a customer's own instance through the user authorization code flow.

--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:

findings.title: Request api_v3 for the standard API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is assumed when no scope is checked. It is a broad grant rather than a work-package-only scope.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when registering the OAuth application for the standard API.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Token boundary is broader than read-only
findings.detail: The documented api_v3 grant does not establish read-only enforcement. The work package list is a GET endpoint, but the boundary must be verified from the granted access and outgoing request log.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the access token used for work package reads.

steps.title: Authorize the representative test user
steps.detail: Sign in as the representative test user on the test instance, grant consent, and exchange the returned code for an access token. Boundary check: confirm the consent request lists the api_v3 scope and the token response contains access_token and expires_in, without calling any write endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: An access token is stored for the test user only.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.

"expires_in" : 7200 ,

steps.title: Read the first page of work package titles
steps.detail: Call the work package list with the OAuth bearer token and read the subject of each element in _embedded.elements. Boundary check: use only GET; confirm the request log shows no POST, PATCH or DELETE and that returned subjects match work packages visible to the test user.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns subject values for the test user's visible work packages.

steps.doneWhen: All pages are retrieved when no nextByOffset link remains and the counts match the total.
